clue.text: A stubborn type beginning to trust a lucky charm

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
a mule is proverbially obstinate
opening letter of trust

explanation.surface: Someone obstinate who is starting to have faith in a good-luck token.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a small object worn as a protective talisman, a synonym for a lucky charm.

clue.text: Sadly it's a threat, if the situation stays as it is

definitions.text: if the situation stays as it is

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so these letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy warning that nothing will change unless action is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at this rate' means if things carry on in the present way.

clue.text: Just out of bed? Correct

blocks.note: first meaning: standing vertically rather than lying down
second meaning: honest and morally proper

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a playful definition of standing up; the second is the moral sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means erect, as one is on getting up, and also honourable or virtuous in conduct.

clue.text: New titles composed for famous bass guitarist

indicators.note: to compose is to put together in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh song names written for a well-known rock bassist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' fits the musical surface, but signals the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: John Entwistle was the bass guitarist of the rock band The Who, renowned for his playing.

clue.text: Drink one with a girl after time

indicators.note: after places the earlier words' pieces behind the time abbreviation, which therefore goes in front

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Having one drink with a girlfriend once closing time has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after time' puts the abbreviation for time first, ahead of the one, the A and the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee liqueur, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Popular group struggling badly

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
Dire Straits, the British rock band

explanation.surface: A well-loved band is having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: Dire Straits was a British rock group of the 1980s led by Mark Knopfler.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in dire straits is an idiom for being in serious trouble or difficulty.

clue.text: Note small car on motorway

blocks.note: the Mini is a famous small British car
M is the prefix of British motorways, as in M1

explanation.surface: Spotting a little car driving along a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note lasting half a semibreve, a half note in American usage.

clue.text: Earnings, extremely remunerative on location

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so just the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of remunerative
a venue is a place where something happens

explanation.surface: Income that pays very well is earned on site.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income received, especially by a business or government, so earnings.

clue.text: Supporter in mass meeting, losing head

indicators.note: to lose one's head is to lose the top, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: a rally is a large public gathering

explanation.surface: A backer at a big demonstration loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone who cooperates with and backs another, a synonym for supporter.

clue.text: Choked, the lord upset about IOM race

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled
about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround what follows

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A peer, upset over the Isle of Man motorbike race, is lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, whose famous road race is the TT (Tourist Trophy).
explanation.definitionFit: To be throttled is to be strangled or have the windpipe squeezed, the same as choked.

clue.text: Celebrity bid stupidly to secure old undergarment

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it without order or sense, so these letters are jumbled
securing something means holding it fast inside, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A famous person bids foolishly at auction for some vintage underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the O held inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberty bodice was a warm vest-like garment worn under clothes by British children in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Unusual paperback?

blocks.note: first meaning: new and out of the ordinary
second meaning: a book of fiction, which a paperback may be

explanation.surface: Remarking on an odd-looking softcover book.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a paperback is only one example of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning original or fresh, and a noun for a long work of prose fiction.

clue.text: I frame Swedish director seducing new Swedish actress

indicators.note: to seduce is to take someone in, so the earlier pieces close around the next one

blocks.note: taken as written
a grid is a framework of bars
N is the abbreviation for new
Ingmar Bergman, the Swedish film director

explanation.surface: An actress says she frames a Swedish director who is seducing a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: I and GRID together take in N, and the director's surname follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid Bergman was the Swedish-born film star of Casablanca, so she is a Swedish actress.

clue.text: Pleased about half-sister being true to priniciples

indicators.note: half of a word means only its first three letters of six survive
about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the shortened one

blocks.note: content means satisfied
taken as written, then cut in half

explanation.surface: Glad that a half-sibling sticks to her convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-sister' looks like a relative, but 'half' is an instruction that keeps SIS. The clue misprints 'principles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Consistent means acting in the same way over time, so steadily faithful to one's principles.

clue.text: Device that spins to and fro

indicators.note: a word that works to and fro reads identically forwards and backwards

blocks.note: a machine part that turns round

explanation.surface: Describing a machine that turns round and swings back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the only source of letters; 'to and fro' adds that the answer is the same in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is anything that rotates, so a device that spins fits directly.

clue.text: Drink, more bubbly, for top boss

indicators.note: bubbly suggests something fizzing and churning, so these letters are stirred up

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
the letters of more rearranged

explanation.surface: Pour more champagne for the chief executive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne, but it is the anagram signal for the word after 'Drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, an informal word for the top boss.

clue.text: Royal taken over to northern university

blocks.note: a prince is a royal
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A royal is driven up to a university in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken over' puts the royal above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League university in New Jersey, USA.

clue.text: Hear about old shocking event

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word's letters go around the second's

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case
aged means old

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen to an account of some long-ago scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is in its legal sense: a court hears, or tries, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a disastrous happening causing great distress, so a shocking event.

clue.text: Further loan

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to promote or move forward
second meaning: money paid ahead of time

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as 'another loan', but 'Further' is a verb meaning to promote.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance a cause is to further it, and an advance is money lent or paid early.

clue.text: Brief increase in small dried grapes

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: raising is increasing
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A short rise in the stocks of little sultanas.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisins are grapes that have been dried, a direct synonym for the definition.

clue.text: Cut off, one very much overdue

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
so means very, as in so good
late means behind time

explanation.surface: Someone is cut off because their bill is badly in arrears.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate or set apart, the verb sense of cut off.

clue.text: Medal winner? Initial clue required?

blocks.note: surface reading: a champion is asked for a hint to get started
setter's reading: the award is known by two initials, the first naming a queen and the second a cross shape

explanation.walkthrough: The award is usually written as two initials, VC, which holders put after their names; the clue plays on needing initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military decoration for gallantry, a medal.

clue.text: A dog may be company on rig at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so these letters are muddled

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
the letters of rig rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet dog might keep a worker company on an offshore oil platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' suits the oil-rig scene but signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed, famously the Queen's favourite, so it is a dog.

clue.text: Prophet from Arabia - Moses?

indicators.note: from here means taken out of the following words, which contain the letters in sequence

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Asking whether a prophet out of Arabia is Moses.
explanation.walkthrough: Moses is a tempting prophet, but the answer is concealed spanning both names.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a Hebrew prophet whose book is among the minor prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Child about to leave Mediterranean island

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters are taken out of the island's name

blocks.note: CA, circa, is Latin for about
the Balearic island

explanation.surface: A youngster is about to depart from a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to leave' reads as 'soon to go', but 'about' is the CA that leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a person under the legal age of adulthood, so a child.

clue.text: Not fully satisfied, cook eats a tin around one

indicators.note: to cook something up is to fabricate it, so these letters are reworked
around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose what follows

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Still hungry, a cook wolfs down a whole tin of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiate is a literary form of insatiable, describing an appetite never fully satisfied.

clue.text: Copy of short specification - mine smudged

indicators.note: short means cut down, so only the clipped form of the long word is used
a smudged word is smeared out of shape, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: spec is the common short form of specification
the letters of mine rearranged

explanation.surface: A smeared photocopy of a brief technical document of mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a single example or sample representing others of its kind, loosely a copy.

clue.text: Perhaps fly home ahead of party

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
a sect is a faction or party

explanation.surface: Maybe catch a plane home before the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' reads as a verb about travelling, but it is the noun, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly is one kind of insect, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example of the class.
